title: 2008 AMC 10B Problem 7

concepts.label: Power scaling of length, area, and volume

statement: An equilateral triangle of side length \(10\) is completely filled in by non-overlapping equilateral triangles of side length \(1.\) How many small triangles are required?

solutions.text:
The large triangle has side length \(10\) times that of a small triangle, so its area is \(10^2=100\) times as large.

Since the small triangles tile it without overlap, exactly \(100\) of them are required.

Thus, the correct answer is C.
hints: Area scales with the square of the side length
The big triangle has \(10^2\) times the area of a small one
